Hi Danielle — great to meet earlier. Thanks for the clear asks — summary and owners below. Short answer on the top: we can share a redacted pen-test summary and a security packet today, start the vendor questionnaire, and provide SLAs for vuln triage and disclosure. Details: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (Security) for the 12-month period ending 2025-09-30. We have the report through our compliance portal; we'll include the SOC 2 readiness statement in the packet.

2) HIPAA / data residency: Redwood supports HIPAA workloads (BAA available). We offer region-specific hosting in us-west and us-east for PHI isolation; we'll include our controls and BAA onboarding steps.

3) Vendor questionnaire: please send your template (or tag questions in the GCP doc). I'll own the first pass with Neha. Proposed turnaround for initial responses: 5 business days for the standard questionnaire, longer if custom technical evidence is requested.

4) Pen test & vuln SLA (high-level): Neha (cc) will follow up with the formal SLA, but our baseline:
   - Pen test handback (executive summary): provided within 10 business days after vendor submission of draft findings to Redwood.
   - Vulnerability triage: critical & high findings acknowledged within 24 hours; mitigation plan within 10 business days.
   - Disclosure & coordinated disclosure window: 14 calendar days minimum prior to public disclosure.

Attachments I'm sending now: Redwood_Security_Packet_v2.pdf (controls, SOC 2 note, HIPAA summary) and a redacted Redwood_Pentest_Summary_v1.pdf (executive summary, no PII/replicable exploit details).

Next steps I propose:
- I'll upload the two docs and send back the completed questionnaire (5 business days).
- Propose a short kickoff with your security lead next week to align on scope and redaction policy for deeper artifacts (30 min).

Marissa, can you own procurement coordination (MSA/terms)? Neha, can you add details on timeline and scan cadence?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Danielle / Aditya — quick security note and proposed operational windows so expectations are aligned. I'm pasting the operational commitments we follow for customers with pen-test requests and vulnerability management. These are what we'll include in the packet and MSA addendum.

Operational commitments (standard):
- Pen test evidence & handback: we provide an executive handback (redacted summary + remediation status matrix) within 10 business days of vendor delivering findings. Full technical appendices are provided to named contacts under an NDA and with approved redaction.
- Remediation SLA: Critical findings (CVSS >= 9.0 or exploit in the wild): acknowledged within 24 hours, mitigation plan within 5 business days, patching or compensating control within 30 calendar days unless otherwise agreed. High findings: mitigation plan within 10 business days, remediation within 60 calendar days.
- Scan cadence: we run authenticated vulnerability scans quarterly for our core infra and after major releases. Customers can request ad-hoc scans for contractually committed engagements (we'll schedule within 7 business days).
- Disclosure & coordinating with customers: coordinated disclosure window by default is 14 calendar days; we will not publish exploit details during the window. For regulated customers (HIPAA), we offer a longer window if needed to allow regulatory notifications to be prepared.
- Retest and verification: after remediation, we run targeted retest of fixed findings within 10 business days.

Redaction policy highlights: we never provide PoC code or raw exploit chains in customer-facing handbacks. Technical appendices can be shared under NDA and with explicit redaction agreement.

If you want, we can formalize the SLA language into a short addendum for your procurement team.

— Neha
Lead, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
